answer: One concrete rule: price each identity off the funding trail it shares. The first account from a payer posts a flat bond; every further account tracing to that same source climbs a spiral of steeper collateral, so a thousand clones drawn from one purse lock far more capital than a thousand independent funders would. Those stacked bonds form a reef a farm cannot cross cheaply, and any hollow identity with no earned, slashable work history stays rate-capped until real jobs fill it.
